Exact symbolic independent checks of block rank, edge comparisons, and the two real scaling identities
correctness.rationale: The neighborhood-square vectors U_i are independent by invertibility of A(H). In both products the nonzero blocks of x give independent coordinate functionals with independent images, so rank L_x is exactly the number of nonzero blocks. The maximal linear subspaces in the rank-at-most-one locus are thus the individual twin blocks; an isomorphism must permute them and preserve their dimensions. Comparing the nonzero block supports in the images of U_i shows the permutation is an automorphism of H and preserves the weighted degrees. Comparing the coefficient in a neighboring block gives F(S_j)=lambda_i S_sigma(j) for every edge ij. Each lambda_i is positive since a nonzero real coordinate vector has positive squared norm. On a block F is a similitude with squared factor lambda_i d_i; evaluating it on S_i gives s_i^2=lambda_i d_i. The edge relations propagate lambda along even walks, giving a single class in the connected nonbipartite case and the two sides in the connected bipartite case. This forces regularity or biregularity. Conversely the given positive cube-root scalings satisfy c_P^2/d_P=c_Q and c_Q^2/d_Q=c_P, and the constant-degree scaling by d is immediate. For K_k the quotient is invertible and k>=3 gives a triangle, so degree n-a_i is constant exactly when part sizes are equal. The adjacency rank of the blow-up is k and nullity is n-k.
residual_risks: No assertion for singular base adjacency or about all nonzero homomorphisms. The packaged rank tests are finite samples; their numerical scale checks use isclose, whereas the proof establishes the exact scaling identities.

value.rationale: The hypothesis isolates a natural structural class of singular graphs, not a numerical cutoff: twin duplication allows arbitrarily high adjacency nullity even on a fixed quotient. Intrinsically recognizing the twin blocks through multiplication ranks gives a useful mechanism explaining rigidity, and the classification captures complete multipartite and other families without enumerating isomorphisms. This is intrinsic significance; it does not overcome exact catalogue coverage.
residual_risks: The frozen theorem does not resolve singular quotients or classify arbitrary homomorphisms.
